newsitem.title: USA: AOL faces suit seeking more than $100 mln.
newsitem.headline: AOL faces suit seeking more than $100 mln.

text.p: America Online Inc will be the target of another class action lawsuit, which is seeking damages in excess of $100 million, said attorneys who are filing the lawsuit in federal court in Los Angeles Thursday.
Bruce Fishelman of Standbury & Fishelman Inc in Los Angeles said his law firm is filing a lawsuit against the online services provider due to its recent network access problems.
The suit, which is filed under the RICO (Racketeering Influence and Corrupt Organization) Act, alleges AOL violated the public interest in connection with its online services.
The suit will also seek to prevent AOL from failing to protect the privacy and intellectual property rights of its members who post their own content, messages, or art on AOL.
FIshelmen said the suit, which is being filed on behalf of AOL's more than eight million members, also seeks to force AOL to comply with the Federal Communications Act as a common carrier.
He said the suit also will seek to force AOL to comply with the Federal Communications Act as a common carrier and that it has damaged subscribers and the public.
AOL has been hit with numerous lawsuits since it switched its members to unlimited access last December and its network could not support the deluge of members seeking access.
An America Online spokeswoman in Dulles, Va. said AOL had not yet been served with the suit, so she could not comment.

"We are addressing the whole subject of what happened in the cyberspace traffic jam in a much different light," said Fishelman. The law firm said it will host a press conference in Hollywood, Calif. on Friday to discuss the suit.
